plans.variant_facts:
The merchandise under consideration is a pipe assembly.. The product of CBP ruling N358639, as its facts describe it. The pipe assembly. is assembled in Mexico using components sourced from Mexico and South Korea.

The steel pipes and flange are produced in Mexico. The brackets are sourced from South Korea. 

In Mexico, the steel pipes and flange will be produced in-house: make the steel pipes, flange.

Final assembly in Mexico: assemble the parts into the finished good.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift or (b) essential character of the Mexican steel pipes and flange
prediction.decisive_step: Manufacturing the steel pipes and flange and assembling the pipe assembly in Mexico
prediction.reasoning: Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(1) and (a)(2), the pipe assembly is not wholly obtained or produced exclusively from domestic materials due to the South Korean brackets. Under 102.11(a)(3), the South Korean brackets undergo the required tariff shift under 102.20 when assembled with the Mexican-produced steel pipes and flange into the finished pipe assembly in Mexico. Even if the tariff shift rule failed, under 102.11(b) the Mexican steel pipes and flange impart the essential character. Thus, the country of origin is Mexico.

verdict.reasoning: In N353124, CBP determined the country of origin of a steel pipe assembly with welded brackets across multiple scenarios. CBP held that origin is conferred in the country where the steel pipe is produced, and that subsequent joining to foreign brackets and assembly does not constitute a substantial transformation. When the pipe was produced in China and brackets/assembly in Mexico, origin was China; when the pipe was produced in Mexico and assembled in Mexico with foreign brackets, origin was Mexico. Moving production of the steel pipes and flange from South Korea to Mexico shifts origin from South Korea to Mexico.

prediction.decisive_step: Production of components and final assembly in Mexico exclusively from Mexican materials
prediction.reasoning: Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(1) and (a)(2), the country of origin is the country where the good is wholly obtained or produced, or produced exclusively from domestic materials. Here, all components (steel pipes, flange, and brackets) are produced in Mexico and assembled into the finished pipe assembly in Mexico without any foreign materials mentioned. Therefore, the country of origin is Mexico under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(2) (or 102.11(a)(1)).

verdict.reasoning: In Variant A, the steel pipes, flange, and brackets are manufactured in South Korea and merely assembled in Mexico, so origin remains South Korea where the essential pipe and fitting components are produced (consistent with pipe assembly rulings such as N345836 where the pipes impart the essential character). In Variant B, the production of all components—the steel pipes, flange, and brackets—moves to Mexico alongside final assembly. Because the entire manufacturing of the constituent steel pipes, flange, brackets, and the finished assembly now occurs in Mexico, the country of origin changes to Mexico.
